examples: expect ("t1", Path("/a")) ⇒ Some(UserId("alice"))  given grants = List(Grant(UserId("alice"), Path("/a"))), sessions.bind(Map("t1" -> UserId("alice")).get)  — Alice's token and a grant for /a: she gets in
expect ("t1", Path("/b")) ⇒ None  given grants = List(Grant(UserId("alice"), Path("/a"))), sessions.bind(Map("t1" -> UserId("alice")).get)  — no grant for /b: refused
reject ("t1", Path("/b")) ⇒ Some(UserId("alice"))  given grants = List(Grant(UserId("alice"), Path("/a"))), sessions.bind(Map("t1" -> UserId("alice")).get)  — access without a grant is never given

reject ("t2", Path("/a")) ⇒ Some(UserId("alice"))  given grants = List(Grant(UserId("alice"), Path("/a"))), sessions.bind(Map("t1" -> UserId("alice")).get)  — a token that is not Alice's never acts for her

content.idea:
# Auth

A system decides which users may access which resources. No user may ever
access a resource they are not authorized to access.

Users identify themselves with tokens they receive at login. Authorization is
given by a table of grants: a user may access a path when a grant names that
user and that path.
content.notModelled:
- How tokens are issued at login, and when they expire.
- Who may change the table of grants.
